updates.text: For any task that requires a heated object to be placed (e.g., 'hot X' or 'heat some X and put it ...'): (1) Acquire the exact named target category; do not pick up a visually similar but different category (such as a cup when a mug is requested) and, if the exact target is not yet visible, continue the systematic search instead of settling for a substitute. (2) Carry it to the microwave; if the microwave is closed, open it once. (3) With the target held at the open microwave, issue exactly one 'heat <target> with microwave 1' action. Do not repeatedly move the target into and out of the microwave and do not loop open/close actions; those steps are wasted and can consume the step budget. (4) Immediately after the successful heat action, go to the requested destination, open it if closed, and place the target there. Do not wander to unrelated cabinets or return to the microwave. (5) Stop once the heated target has been placed.

For any task requiring more than one instance of a target category ('two X', 'find two X', etc.): (1) Treat the initial room listing as the search set and inspect each receptacle type at least once: open every closed cabinet, drawer, and fridge encountered, and also check open furniture surfaces such as countertops, diningtables, coffeetables, shelves, dressers, beds, sofas, sidetables, tvstands, armchairs, and desks; do not restrict the sweep to one furniture type (for example, only shelves and drawers) while other listed receptacles remain unchecked. (2) When a location is visibly empty or an object there has already been moved, go to a different not-yet-inspected receptacle rather than immediately re-checking the same empty container; do not cycle among a small set of already-inspected locations. (3) After delivering one instance to the destination, resume the sweep for the next instance from unvisited receptacles instead of stopping at one or rechecking emptied ones. (4) Continue until the requested number of instances of the exact category has been placed; do not substitute another category to reach the count. (5) Stop once the required count is placed.

updates.text: Search rule for tasks whose exact target is not initially visible: run a single forward sweep that does not oscillate. Treat each inspected receptacle as consumed; the next move should go to a different receptacle, ideally one not just inspected. Use the numbered receptacle names as a local progress cue: after checking an instance of a family, prefer the next higher-numbered unvisited instance or a wholly uninspected family or surface instead of jumping back to an earlier location. Open each closed container once and read its contents; if it is empty, continue forward to a new receptacle rather than cycling back through earlier ones. Include cheap surface checks (countertops, desks, beds, tables, shelves) early in the sweep. Continue until the exact requested category is found or all plausible receptacles have been inspected once, keeping within the step budget.

Conditioning rule for tasks that require the exact target to be cooled or heated: after acquiring the target, go to the required appliance (fridge for cool, microwave for heat) and open it if closed. Perform the cool/heat action directly on the held target while at the open appliance; holding the target is sufficient in the observed environment. If the conditioning action is not offered for the held target, place the target inside once and perform the action, but never replace conditioning with repeated close/open or remove/reinsert cycles. Perform one conditioning action, then carry the target to the requested destination (opening it if closed) and place it there. If the conditioning appliance is also the destination, condition the target and then place it there.

Quantity rule for ordinary multi-instance placement: when the task requires two or more instances of the exact category, deliver them sequentially. After placing the first exact instance at the destination, continue searching (from remaining uninspected receptacles or a known source) for another instance of the same exact category and repeat until the requested count is placed. Do not stop after one, do not substitute a differently named near-match, and do not apply the desklamp rule of finishing with one co-located target to ordinary multi-instance put tasks.
